title: Record Stock Movements
readerIntent: Record auditable increases, decreases, releases, receipts, and corrections.
priorKnowledge: Know balance, unit, reason, source document, and idempotency.
summary: Movements are immutable business evidence that change balances through governed services and concurrency controls.

sections.heading: Rules
items: Use stable movement type, reason, tenant, product/variant, warehouse/pool, quantity/unit, reference, actor, time, revision, and idempotency key.
Never edit history to hide a correction; create a compensating movement.
Reject incompatible units, negative results where prohibited, duplicates, unauthorized sources, and stale balances.
Update derived availability/cache/events only after the authoritative movement commits.

sections.heading: Movement types
items: Receipt and issue.
Reservation, release, allocation, and deallocation effects where represented.
Transfer dispatch and receipt.
Return, damage, quarantine, release, loss, and adjustment.
Project-defined types added through Inventory extension contracts.

sections.heading: Immutable ledger principle
paragraphs: A movement records what occurred and why. Corrections create a linked compensating movement; editing history destroys reconciliation and audit evidence.
Derived balances can be rebuilt from movements and governed opening evidence according to the model contract.

sections.heading: Example
paragraphs: A warehouse receives 25.5 kilograms of produce. Later 0.5 kilograms are damaged. Inventory records a receipt movement followed by a damage movement using compatible Units definitions.
Availability reflects the resulting eligible balance; the damage record is not erased or silently subtracted.

sections.heading: Concurrency and unknown outcomes
items: Use balance revision or qualified atomic operation.
Use stable external reference and idempotency key.
Reject prohibited negative balance.
On timeout, reconcile by identity before retry.
Publish derived effects only after commit.

sections.heading: Verification and observability
items: Every movement type and compatible unit.
Duplicate, stale revision, unauthorized source, and wrong tenant.
High-contention updates without lost movement.
Compensation and reconciliation.
Balance, availability, cache, event, publishing, and audit integration.
Throughput, conflict, failure, reason, and unknown-outcome metrics.

sections.heading: Retention and export
paragraphs: Movement evidence follows business retention and authorized export policy. Bulk extracts use Inventory services and never dump provider storage or cache as the ledger.

sections.heading: Operator decision
items: When balance and movement evidence disagree, stop unsafe adjustment, preserve correlation and idempotency identity, and use reconciliation rather than editing the balance directly.
A timed-out command remains uncertain until queried or reconciled; repeating it without the same idempotency key can duplicate stock.
Alert on failed movements, negative-balance prevention, unexplained adjustment volume, and projection lag with warehouse-safe bounded dimensions.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How Stock Movements Work
paragraphs: Use Stock Movements when a business event changes the on-hand quantity of an item in a Warehouse or Warehouse Location. Examples include receiving goods, issuing goods, correcting a count, recording damage, or completing one leg of a transfer.

sections.heading: What A Business User Needs To Know
paragraphs: Nodics records both the new balance and evidence of the attempted change. A repeated request with the same key does not change stock twice. Concurrent changes cannot silently overwrite one another because only the request holding the expected revision may update the balance.
items: the enterprise and Warehouse context;
the item being changed;
an exact quantity and Unit;
a movement type and business reason;
an idempotency key supplied by the calling process; and
the Stock Balance revision previously read by that process.

sections.heading: Quantity And Unit Rules
paragraphs: Quantities are stored and calculated as exact decimal strings, supporting pieces, weight, liquid volume, land area, and other Units dimensions without floating-point drift. A movement may use another compatible Unit: for example, `1000 G` can be normalized into a `KG` balance. Units selects an active direct or inverse exact factor, applies geography and enterprise scope, and rejects incompatible, ambiguous, unavailable, or forbidden-rounding cases before Inventory changes stock.

sections.heading: Operational Recovery
paragraphs: If a node stops after changing a balance but before finalizing its movement record, retry the same request with the same idempotency key. Nodics recognizes the balance evidence and finishes the movement without applying it again.
Do not manually edit Stock Balance records. Corrections must be new movements with a reason so the audit history remains explainable.

sections.heading: Current Scope
paragraphs: The implemented capability is the exact on-hand ledger with modular exact Unit conversion. Reservations, allocations, available-to-sell, sourcing, coordinated transfers, BackOffice screens, and public Stock APIs are not part of this slice.
Developers and operators should read the Inventory module's [Stock Core contract](/docs/reference/commerce) for configuration, extension rules, failure codes, and verification.
